articles.title: Scherzetto review – Toni Servillo brings gravitas to a dithering Neapolitan ghost story
articles.summary: Venice film festival The Venice fixture plays an illustrator haunted by his boyhood in Mario Martone’s part spooky, part sentimental oddity. It’s always good to see the veteran Italian star Toni Servillo at Venice; in fact, the festival is pretty much unthinkable without him.
body: Daniele (played by Servillo) is a septuagenarian book illustrator whose old-fashioned, hand-drawn artistry is something he testily treasures. He has come back to his family home in Naples, to the gloomy apartment where he was brought up, just behind the train station, and where his grownup daughter Betta (Serena Rossi) now lives with her husband and their five-year-old son Mario (newcomer Lorenzo Perrotta), who is adorable and as bright as a button, but also borderline insufferable.

And so the film continues, weirdly toggling between the uncanny and the sweetly sentimental – although the tougher, more wised-up sense of the city itself comes across with Daniele and Mario’s walks through the streets. It’s a baffling misfire.

articles.title: Steve Carell Almost Played ‘The Office’ Creator Greg Daniels’ Dad in Biopic About the 1968 Olympics
articles.summary: Steve Carell and writer Greg Daniels got so close while making “The Office,” they became like family. So much so that Daniels once wanted Carell to play his dad Aaron in a biopic he wrote about him almost 20 years ago. “He’s a very colorful person and he actually was in the Olympics in 1968,
body: “He had a very rare sport. That’s how he was able to do it,” Daniels explained. “It was the demonstration sport of Mexico, basically like jai alai but with paddles and so he managed to wrangle his way in with some friends.”
The elder Daniels competed as an amateur athlete in the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City.

Carell, along with Conan O’Brien, spoke at the star unveiling. “Everyone told me not to do ‘The Office,’” Carell said. “[They said] it will not work. The original is too good. It is a waste of time. And mostly, it is just going to stink. And then a crazy thing happened. It didn’t stink because of Greg Daniels.”

During our chat, Daniels put the kibosh on fans’ hopes for any sort of “Office” revival or reboot. “I don’t think we need to find out what all the characters are doing so much because of the way the show ended,” he said. “It seemed like people liked the ending and you’re just sort of risking a lot to open it up again.”

articles.title: James Talarico Blasts ‘Government Censorship’ After ABC Pulls His Jimmy Kimmel Interview Over FCC Concerns: ‘Dangerous Form of Cancel Culture’
articles.summary: James Talarico, the Democratic candidate running for senator in Texas, has spoken out after ABC pulled his sit-down with Jimmy Kimmel over FCC concerns. The interview will instead be posted to the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” YouTube channel on Thursday night.
body: He told Symone Sanders Townsend of MS NOW’s “The Weeknight” that he still has hope ABC will air the Kimmel interview across its broadcast channels. “I’m still hopeful that we can have this interview on the air,” he said. “So we’ll see what happens tonight.

Kimmel announced on his show Wednesday night that ABC had decided to preempt his chat with Talarico because of concerns about Trump’s FCC, which is led by Brendan Carr. The government agency is currently locked in a dispute with ABC over whether “The View” qualifies as a “bona fide news program” exempt from the “equal time” rule. The FCC also played a key role in Kimmel’s brief suspension in 2025 over Charlie Kirk comments.

“Out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense, my interview tomorrow with James Talarico will not air on television,” Kimmel said on his show Wednesday night.

Ultimately, Colbert put his Talarico interview on YouTube, with the clip garnering 9.5 million views. The Talarico campaign raised $2.5 million in the 24 hours after Colbert revealed he was barred from airing the interview.

articles.title: Tony Gatlif obituary
articles.summary: Algerian-born French director of more than 20 films that celebrated Roma culture. The French film director Tony Gatlif, who has died aged 77, was regularly described as “cinema’s Gypsy auteur”, so often did his films focus on Roma communities and their music.
body: Latcho Drom conveys the centuries-long migration from Asia to western Europe of a nomadic people we now call Gypsies or Roma, as a fable told entirely in images and music. There is no voiceover, talking heads or text; instead Gatlif lets the striking settings and musical performances enchant viewers. It is an idealised portrait of the Roma, not a documentary (as some labelled it), and while Gatlif portrays the discrimination and persecution Roma communities experience, his emphasis was on celebrating Roma beauty and artistry.

After the success of Latcho Drom, Gatlif went on to write and direct a feature film every couple of years, his most recent being Ange (2025). These films were all dramas and tended to focus either on a Roma community – Mondo (1995), Gadjo Dilo (1997), Vengo (2000), Swing (2001), Korkoro (2009) – or were road movies in which the protagonists drift across France, then head into eastern Europe or North Africa, seeking meaning and origins. His 2004 film Exils won Gatlif the best director award at the Cannes film festival.

The French film director Tony Gatlif, who has died aged 77, was regularly described as “cinema’s Gypsy auteur”, so often did his films focus on Roma communities and their music.

articles.title: The Legend of Patricia Summersett’s ‘Zelda’: Voice Actress Behind Nintendo’s Iconic Princess on Franchise’s 40th Anniversary, Upcoming Live-Action Movie
articles.summary: “The Legend of Zelda” turns 40 this year, but the titular princess at the center of the franchise doesn’t look a day over whatever ethereal age the Nintendo video game franchise needs her to be for any given game.
body: In addition to “Breath of the Wild,” Summersett has also voiced Zelda in “Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity,” “The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom and “Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment,” but can’t confirm one way or another yet if she’s involved in the upcoming “Ocarina of Time” remake set to release in November, or if she has anything to do with the live-action “Zelda” movie slated for April 2027.
And though she has done additional video-game voice acting and on-screen roles, Summersett says playing Zelda is one of the most physically comfortable experiences in her career.

“Yes, actually, it takes a little warming up for me to get into any range that it’s going to sit at, but I always feel a sense of deep relaxation after the recording sessions because it’s soft and you have to be kind of relaxed when you’re hitting that range,” Summersett says. “Even if she’s a thoughtful, heady character, the voice itself has to remain relaxed. So you get a sense of feeling very, very nice and warm afterward. Also, holding your center of energy at a sort of young, wide-eyed, youthful place that has a big heart is a pleasant feeling. Not all characters get to be like that.”

articles.title: NAZA review – Israeli intelligence officers cast chilling light on civilian deaths
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Under the cover of night, anonymous personnel discuss AI, error rates and problematic intelligence units in a documentary produced by the Guardian.
body: There are flaws: interviews were conducted on the condition of anonymity, but if no-one can be persuaded to put their name and face to their words (and of course it is terribly dangerous) then the impact of this as testimony is lessened. But even so, the film is casting a chilling light on what is happening now in Gaza.

Their faces in shadow, appearances and voices digitally altered, disillusioned Israeli intelligence officers and personnel speak to the directors about the war in Gaza. They do this semi-furtively on the dark night-time rooftops of Tel Aviv, the home of Israeli intelligence, supposedly for journalistic secrecy purposes – but it also provides a dramatic backdrop, as well as ambient footage of the city in all its eerie heedlessness and heartlessness. Periodically, the camera’s eye will drift across the gleaming apartment buildings, zooming in on glimpses of prosperous lives just 60km from Gaza.

articles.title: The Odyssey and Spider-Man propel record-breaking summer box office worldwide
articles.summary: The biggest May to September of all time was recorded in US cinemas, with the UK enjoying a 56% rise in audiences, outstripped by an 88% lift in the Middle East and Africa.
body: As well as celebrating their wedding, the actors Tom Holland and Zendaya have something else to toast: their two summer blockbusters – The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day – have officially made box office history.
The films were credited as the driving force behind the US’s biggest summer season of all time, taking $4.761bn (£3.51bn) from 1 May-7 September, beating 2013’s $4.756bn.

Spider-Man is currently on $2.4bn worldwide and likely to climb higher, while The Odyssey has made $1.6bn. Other key titles driving sales include Toy Story 5, Michael and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, all of which have grossed over $1bn.

The breadth of the success of Destin Daniel Cretton’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day was a particular surprise. The film is the best-performing of the year so far and the third highest-grossing film of all time. Its opening weekend was the second-best of all time behind Avengers: Endgame (2019) and it is also the second-fastest film to gross $1bn, doing so in six days.

articles.title: Esther Rantzen says she is too fragile to travel to Switzerland to end life
articles.summary: The broadcaster and campaigner says she missed her chance to go before living with cancer became "unbearable".
body: Dame Esther Rantzen has said she is now "too physically fragile" to travel to Switzerland to end her life at an assisted suicide clinic.

The veteran broadcaster, 86, said she would have to fly to the country, where the practice is legal, alone, which she could only have done before her life became "unbearable" and before she was ready to end her life.
The Childline founder, who is terminally ill with cancer, first revealed in December 2023 that she had joined the Dignitas clinic.

Dame Esther used her statement on Thursday to reiterate a plea for MPs to vote in favour of legalising assisted dying in England and Wales when proposed legislation is revisited by Parliament on Friday.

articles.title: Why George Lucas’ Museum Building Mogs LACMA’s New David Geffen Exhibition Hall
articles.summary: The mogul-auteur’s billion-dollar new L.A. cultural center marks a stark contrast with recent failures, involving substantial public money, at the encyclopedic art museum across town.
body: The new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is a Rorschach test for the value of mass culture, the future of Los Angeles and the legacy of founder George Lucas. Its arrival also happens to highlight LACMA ’s epic flop of a main new exhibition hall, the David Geffen Galleries building, which debuted across town four months ago.

LACMA’s failures, involving substantial public money, constitute serious lapses. Its director Michael Govan sits on the Lucas Museum’s board. Lucas’ wife, the prominent executive Mellody Hobson, who was a driving force on his project, is in turn a LACMA board member. Govan might prevail on Lucas to join as well, as an idiosyncratic and dyspeptic if public-minded voice. Perhaps Lucas could replace one of the seats still somehow held by the moguls Casey Wasserman and Steve Tisch, who of late have each had to relinquish ownership from their respective business enterprises following revelations of their connections to the sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.

articles.title: ‘Zero Intention of Living Quietly’ Review: Doc About ‘A Different Man’ Star Adam Pearson Is Moving, When It’s Not Getting in Its Own Way
articles.summary: The Telluride debut centers on the friendship between the actor, who has facial disfigurement from neurofibromatosis, and a teenage girl with the same genetic condition.
body: At some point in the last 10 to 15 years, the phrase “representation matters” crossed over, at least for me, from a key directive to a tired cliché. I’d grown frustrated by the way some took it to mean that merely putting a (LGBTQ/POC/poor/disabled/what have you) person onscreen was the end goal rather than a first step; the accompanying pressure for those marginalized communities to “feel seen” by these depictions; the implication that making people “feel seen” should be art’s loftiest ambition in the first place.

Directed by Edward Lovelace, the film serves as a loose memoir for Pearson. Footage of his present life is interspersed with old photos and home movies and film and television clips to chronicle his experience with neurofibromatosis and his intermittent career as a performer — from talent shows in his youth (including, delightfully, one performance in which he’s dressed as Avril Lavigne), to his breakout role at 26 in 2013’s Under the Skin and subsequent reality TV appearances, to his even bigger second breakout in 2024’s A Different Man.
